THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Lift Drizzle

Five ingredients. Bright + salty + fermented + hot. Acid does the lift.

YIELD2 servings
TOTAL TIME2 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~140 cal | ~1.5g protein

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp olive oil (California Organic Extra Virgin, or any quality EVOO)
  • 2 tbsp Kikkoman All-Purpose Soy Sauce
  • 1 tbsp Red Boat Fish Sauce 40°N

Ingredients — continued

  • 3 tbsp ReaLemon lemon juice (~6 portions, or fresh-squeezed from 1 lemon)
  • 1/2 tsp Deep Coriander Powder
  • 2 fresh red Thai chilies, finely chopped

You've made something soft + rich (pork mince, fatty chicken, creamy noodle) and the dish is dying for acid + salt + heat. Lift Drizzle is what separates 'healthy protein in a vehicle' from 'restaurant-grade dinner.' The name says it — acid lifts.

Method

  1. 1.WHISK IN A SMALL BOWL. Olive oil + soy sauce + fish sauce + lemon juice + coriander powder. Whisk until the coriander dissolves (it tries to clump — keep whisking).
  2. 2.ADD CHILIES. Chop 2 fresh red Thai chilies finely. Stir in. The chili oil + capsaicin needs to mingle for ~2 min before serving — they're not just visual.
  3. 3.TASTE + ADJUST. Too salty → bump lemon by 1 tsp. Too flat → add 1 more pinch coriander. Too thin / runny — DON'T thicken with cornstarch (that's the takeout trap). Add 1 more tsp olive oil if you want body, but flat-and-bright is the brand.
  4. 4.SERVE. Small bowl with a small spoon. Adults spoon into their wraps / bowls / salads at the table. Never pour over the platter — lettuce wilts in 60 sec.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

If something fails

Drizzle tastes flat / one-dimensional: You skipped the coriander OR under-measured the lemon. Coriander adds the third layer of brightness past lemon + chilies. Bump lemon by 1 tsp + add 1/4 tsp more coriander.

Too salty: Soy and fish sauce both stack salt. Add 1 tbsp more lemon juice to rebalance. Don't dilute with water — kills the body.

Too oily / heavy mouthfeel: LIGHTER VARIANT: drop olive oil to 1 tbsp + bump lemon to 4 tbsp + add 1 tsp rice vinegar + 1 tsp allulose. Brighter, half the calories, slightly sweetened to balance the soy. Try both, pick your tier.

Not enough heat: Bump to 3 chilies, OR stir in 1/2 tsp Dynasty Sesame Chili Oil. Don't reach for sambal — too thick, kills the pourable consistency.

Sauce separated after sitting: Olive oil + acid always separates. Whisk again before serving. Or shake in a small jar. The separation isn't a flaw — it's the structure.

Storage and reheating

Store: Small jar with a lid. Fridge. Stays bright + clean 5 days. Shake before serving — separation is normal.

Reheat: Cold or room temp only. Heat kills the brightness + breaks the olive oil.

Lasts: 5 days refrigerated. Make fresh per meal if you can — takes 2 min. Pre-batch if you're eating this dinner across the week.

Estimated nutrition

~140 cal | ~1.5g protein.

Per-serving (140 cal / 3.2g protein / 13.5g fat / 2.2g carbs) computed by MacroFactor from logged ingredients: 2 servings × 53g sauce per serving. 13.5g of that fat is from the 2 tbsp olive oil — this is the oil-heavy version. The lighter variant (1 tbsp oil + 4 tbsp lemon + 1 tsp rice vinegar + tiny allulose) drops per-serving to ~80 cal / 7g fat. Both versions live here; the shipped version is the richer one because olive oil carries salt onto lettuce better than thinner sauces.

Flavor target

Bright + salty + fermented + lightly spicy. Acid leads; oil carries; coriander aromatic finishes. NOT sweet, NOT sticky, NOT creamy. If you stir it and it looks like ranch or hoisin glaze, you've gone wrong.

Adult plate | Kid plate

Adult plate

Adult

Full recipe — 2 chopped fresh red chilies + 1/2 tsp coriander + the full base. Serve in a small bowl with a spoon, not poured over the dish. Adults build their own bite.

Kid plate

Kid

Skip the chilies. Skip the coriander. Drop the soy to 1 tbsp. The remaining base (oil + fish sauce + lemon) is approachable but most kids will still prefer a creamier alt — Herdez Taqueria Avocado Cilantro is the better kid sauce. Default to that.

Brands I use

Red Boat
Fish Sauce 40°N (8.45 fl oz)
First-press, barrel-aged Vietnamese fish sauce. Just anchovies + salt — no MSG, no caramel coloring. The salt + umami + fermented depth that lifts the dish without sugar. Three Crabs or Squid Brand work; avoid discount labels.
Kikkoman
All-Purpose Soy Sauce
Clean salt + umami. Reduced sodium also works — drops the salt by ~30%, doesn't change the flavor profile much. The site's default soy.
ReaLemon
100% Lemon Juice (small squeeze bottle)
The acid that does the lift. Fresh-squeezed is better but the bottle stays in the fridge year-round. 3 tbsp is the right dose — less = flat, more = puckers.
Deep
Coriander Powder (Indian grocery brand)
1/2 tsp adds bright citrus-floral aromatic — the third layer past lemon + chilies. Indian grocery store brand, ~$3 a jar. Substitute any pure ground coriander.
